headline_marked: [[Nvidia's RTX Spark Superchip excels in local AI]] on Surface Laptop Ultra, but gaming lags
headline: Nvidia's RTX Spark Superchip excels in local AI on Surface Laptop Ultra, but gaming lags
summary: The top-end Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra features 20 CPU cores, 6144 CUDA cores, and 128GB LPDDR5X-9400 RAM, delivering impressive local AI performance but trailing Apple's M5 Max in CPU benchmarks.
details: Nvidia's RTX Spark platform, announced at Computex 2026, aims to "reinvent the PC" with local AI agents. It pairs the GB10 Superchip with Windows on Arm, developed with partners like Microsoft, Dell, and HP. The goal is to create an autonomous companion for work and creation.
Tom's Hardware tested the platform using Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra, equipped with the full RTX Spark Superchip. This system boasts 20 CPU cores, 6144 CUDA cores, and 128GB of LPDDR5X-9400 RAM.

Initial testing focused on broad platform experience and competitive performance, particularly local AI. System-specific details like battery life or build quality are under a separate embargo and will be released later.
In CPU benchmarks like Geekbench, the MediaTek Arm CPU complex on the Spark platform significantly trails Apple's M5 Max. However, the system still feels responsive in general use.

For local AI performance, a new benchmark called AgentPerf-local was used, developed by Artificial Analysis. This benchmark measures the total time to complete agentic AI tasks, capturing end-to-end performance rather than just prompt processing and token generation.

Tests were conducted with Qwen 3.8-27B and Qwen 3.6 35B A3B mixture-of-experts models, using llama.cpp as the inference backend. The results highlight the platform's strong capabilities in handling complex local AI workloads efficiently.

headline: Amazon's Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $74.99
summary: Bee Frontier ($74.99) and Bee Eclipse ($99.99) leverage AI to transcribe conversations, create summaries, and set actionable to-dos, with optional Amazon and Alexa integration.
details: Amazon's personal AI wearable maker, Bee, has unveiled its first new products since its acquisition last year: the Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse. The Frontier is a wearable device, while the Eclipse is a credit-card-sized device that attaches to smartphones. The Bee Frontier starts at $74.99.
The Bee Frontier is priced significantly lower than competitors like Plaud Note ($159) and Pocket AI ($129). The Bee Eclipse will be available for $99.99. Both devices come in multiple color options.

These new devices continue Bee's core mission: using AI to take notes from daily conversations. They help users remember important details and transform them into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.
Practical applications include remembering agreed-upon dates for social plans and creating calendar invites. Users can also capture lecture notes or medical care plans discussed with doctors.

All Bee devices offer free conversation summaries and 14 days of memory. For $11.99 per month, the Bee Pro subscription provides unlimited summaries, integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party apps, plus suggested to-dos and a personal chat assistant.

Bee prioritizes privacy with a private computing security architecture. Raw audio is processed in real-time and then deleted, ensuring it's not stored. Conversation transcripts are encrypted using device-controlled keys.

This encryption means no one, including Amazon employees, can access your files unless you manually share them. Users can also optionally connect Bee to Alexa, allowing Echo devices to use Voice ID for recording, with the ability to delete transcripts anytime.

New integrations with Amazon.com and Alexa enable users to make purchases directly from Amazon or ask Alexa for Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free. This expands the utility of the devices within the Amazon ecosystem.

Bee also integrates with existing productivity software like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook. This allows it to draft emails, set up meetings, and surface action items. It can also connect with Apple's HealthKit for wellness insights.

Both the Bee Frontier and Eclipse feature a single button for power and an indicator light for active summarizing. The Frontier boasts IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and advanced noise-filtering dual microphones.
The devices are supported by a newly redesigned companion mobile app and a new desktop app. The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, with the Eclipse launching soon.
